Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or other names that have the same functional role as P2TP2A.
(2) The institutional structure of P2TP2A and or other similar names is established by Regent's Decree.
(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names is carried out by adhering to the Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Part Four
Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8 (1) Policy formulation, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through the following mechanism: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with related SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection services for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through the following mechanism:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with related SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent's Regulation.
(4) Policy formulation, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization regarding prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 5
(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families of victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence toward women and children and their families.

Third Part
Institutional Matters

Article 20
(1) Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to administer protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Regional Government

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY, BUSINESS SECTOR

Article 13
In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) that oversees Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

CHAPTER XII
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 24
All forms of operational regulations for the implementation of this Regional Regulation must be in place no later than 6 months after this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated.

2.1.rationale: The judge applied an overly narrow interpretation (requiring cross-jurisdiction/inter-government coordination). In the Indonesian text, the regulation clearly establishes an institutional coordination mechanism within the regency: Pasal 8(1)(b) and 8(2)(b) require “koordinasi dan sinkronisasi” with SKPD terkait for planning and implementation; Pasal 8(5)(a)-(c) mandates forming “jaringan kerja” and coordination/integration/synchronization among “pemangku kepentingan”; and Pasal 13 explicitly appoints an SKPD as “koordinator” for coordinating implementation. These provisions satisfy an institutional network/coordination mechanism indicator even without mentioning other jurisdictions.

4.2.rationale: The judge treated general ‘socialization’ about preventing violence and fulfilling women/children’s rights as equivalent to ‘gender equality education.’ In the Indonesian text, Pasal 8(5)(d) says “melakukan sosialisasi tentang pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan, serta pemenuhan hak-hak anak dan perempuan,” and Pasal 6(1)-(2) discusses increasing “pengetahuan, ketrampilan dan kesadaran” to prevent violence. 5.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text does include religious actors as part of the response system, but the retrieved passages did not surface the clearest evidence. In Pasal 11(b), the local government must provide human resources including “tokoh spiritual” (spiritual/religious figures), which indicates engagement of religious/spiritual leaders as stakeholders in service provision. The candidates shown to the judge included Pasal 9(1)(d) ‘layanan spiritual’ (spiritual services) but not Pasal 11(b)’s explicit inclusion of “tokoh spiritual” as part of the system’s human resources, which would more directly answer an ‘engagement’ indicator. Because the strongest stakeholder-engagement wording was missing from the retrieved set, the judge’s No is understandable given what they saw.

6.1.rationale: The judge over-interpreted a broad inclusion clause as a specific commitment to women in crisis/disaster settings. In the Indonesian text, Pasal 5(1) lists coverage “dalam semua situasi termasuk ... anak dalam situasi darurat” (children in emergency situations) and other vulnerable child categories; it does not specifically address women in crisis settings (e.g., disaster response measures tailored to women, shelters/GBV services in disasters). The phrase “anak dalam situasi darurat” is child-focused, and the rest of the regulation is generally about violence services, not crisis/disaster programming for women. Since the retrieved evidence does not establish women-specific crisis-setting provisions, the predicted Yes reflects overly permissive reasoning.
